title: Descent of compatible maps along a submersive Stein morphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\mathcal U$ an algebraic stack over $k$ as defined in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $V$ an algebraic space over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $p:\mathcal U\to V$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, meaning these properties hold on etale scheme charts of $V$ and its diagonal is quasi-compact. Assume that $p$ is universally submersive, meaning that after every algebraic-space base change $V'\to V$, the continuous map $|\mathcal U\times_VV'|\to|V'|$ [def-sfb-stack-point-topological-space, def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties] is surjective and induces the quotient topology. Assume also that $\mathcal O_V\to p_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ is an isomorphism on the small etale site of $V$, with structure sheaves and direct image as in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Put $R=(\mathcal U\times_V\mathcal U)_{\mathrm{red}}$, the reduced closed substack defined on smooth charts by the nilradical, and let $p_1,p_2:R\to\mathcal U$ be its projections. For every algebraic space $Z/k$ whose diagonal $\Delta_{Z/k}$ is an immersion (locally a closed immersion into an open subspace), precomposition with $p$ is injective on $k$-morphisms, and a morphism $h:\mathcal U\to Z$ is in its image if and only if $hp_1=hp_2$. Morphisms from stacks to spaces are taken up to 2-isomorphism. This statement assumes no condition on the geometric fibres of $p$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.1, proof, printed p.36, exact Hom diagram before the geometric-fibre argument. Its general descent input is Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of etale morphisms, Proposition 7.2 and Theorem 7.4 (weakly normal descent), pp.28--29 in the author PDF https://davidrydh.se/papers/submersion20100305.pdf; the structure-sheaf isomorphism supplies the relative weak-normality condition. The stack formulation uses smooth-chart descent as in Alper. Local Rydh PDF also WANTED. Read arXiv:1005.2398v3 online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First prove uniqueness. If $a,b:V\to Z$ satisfy $ap=bp$, their equalizer $E=V\times_{(a,b),Z\times_kZ,\Delta_Z}Z\to V$ is an immersion: pull back a factorization of $\Delta_Z$ as closed in an open; on charts the closed part is the quotient by the extended ideal. The map $p$ factors through $E$. Surjectivity of $|p|$ makes the underlying image of $E$ all of $V$, so the open part is all of $V$ and $E\hookrightarrow V$ is closed. Its ideal maps to zero in $p_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ and hence is zero by the assumed isomorphism. Thus $E=V$ and $a=b$.

source.place: Theorem (7.4), locally separated case, printed p.29; Alper Proposition 7.1.1 proof, printed p.36. Both read online, local copies WANTED; explicit stack and Stein adaptations by Q49.

proof.text: Fix $h$ satisfying $hp_1=hp_2$. Put $P=Z\times_kV$, $P'=Z\times_k\mathcal U$, with quotient map $t=1_Z\times p:P'\to P$, and graph section $s':\mathcal U\to P'$. Choose an open $N\subseteq Z\times_kZ$ in which the diagonal is closed. Let $A'\subseteq P'$ be the inverse image of $N$ under $(z,u)\mapsto(z,h(u))$. This open and the graph subset $\Gamma'=|s'(\mathcal U)|$ are saturated for $t$: two lifts over the same geometric point of $V$ give a geometric point of $\mathcal U\times_V\mathcal U$, which factors through its reduction, and the hypothesis makes their $h$-values equal. This checks saturation after any common algebraically closed extension, which is precisely equality of points of the fibre products. Thus $t^{-1}(t(A'))=A'$ and $t^{-1}(t(\Gamma'))=\Gamma'$.

source.place: Theorem (7.4), locally separated case, printed p.29; Alper Proposition 7.1.1 proof, printed p.36. Both read online, local copies WANTED; explicit stack and Stein adaptations by Q49.

proof.text: Set $A=t(A')$ and $\Gamma=t(\Gamma')$. Since $t$ induces the quotient topology, $A$ is open in $P$. On $A'$, $s'$ is the pullback of the closed immersion $\Delta_Z:Z\hookrightarrow N$, hence is closed, with image $\Gamma'$. The quotient criterion applied to $A'\to A$ now makes $\Gamma$ closed in $A$. These assertions concern the full graph, not merely a choice of geometric-fibre points. The map $g=(h,p):\mathcal U\to A$ is quasi-compact: it is the composite of the closed section $\mathcal U\hookrightarrow A\times_V\mathcal U=A'$ with the base change $A'\to A$ of the quasi-compact map $p$. On each affine chart, a closed immersion is a quotient of its coordinate ring and is quasi-compact; pullbacks and this composite preserve quasi-compactness by the finite-subcover criterion.

source.place: Theorem (7.4), locally separated case, printed p.29; Alper Proposition 7.1.1 proof, printed p.36. Both read online, local copies WANTED; explicit stack and Stein adaptations by Q49.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-schematic-image-qc] to $g:\mathcal U\to A$. Obtain its closed image $W\hookrightarrow A$, with factor $q:\mathcal U\to W$, $\mathcal O_W\hookrightarrow q_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$, and $|W|=\Gamma$ because $\Gamma$ is already closed. Write $r:W\to V$ for the projection. The identity $rq=p$ holds by construction. The graph section $s':\mathcal U\to A'$ factors through $W\times_V\mathcal U$, since its two components are $q$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal U}$. It is a closed immersion there, and is surjective on underlying spaces by the saturation equality of step 2. On every smooth chart it is therefore a closed immersion defined by an ideal of nilpotents, so it remains a homeomorphism after any base change.

source.place: Theorem (7.4), locally separated case, printed p.29; Alper Proposition 7.1.1 proof, printed p.36. Both read online, local copies WANTED; explicit stack and Stein adaptations by Q49.

proof.text: It follows that $r_{\mathcal U}:W\times_V\mathcal U\to\mathcal U$ is a universal homeomorphism: after any chart and any further base change its composite with the preceding surjective closed section is the identity, and that section is a homeomorphism. To descend these properties, for every space $T\to V$ the map $\mathcal U_T\to T$ is a quotient surjection. For a closed $C\subseteq W_T$, the inverse image of $r_T(C)$ in $\mathcal U_T$ is the image of its closed inverse image under the homeomorphism $r_{\mathcal U_T}$; it is closed. Thus $r_T$ is closed. Its fibres are single points, as can be checked after a common algebraically closed extension and a lift to $\mathcal U_T$. Hence $r$ is a universal homeomorphism. Its diagonal is an immersion by the same diagonal pullback calculation, and is surjective by universal injectivity, so is a closed immersion. Thus $r$ is separated.

source.place: Theorem (7.4), locally separated case, printed p.29; Alper Proposition 7.1.1 proof, printed p.36. Both read online, local copies WANTED; explicit stack and Stein adaptations by Q49.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-separated-space-homeomorphism-affine], $r$ is affine and representable by schemes. Work on any etale affine chart $T=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to V$; write $W_T=\operatorname{Spec}B_1$. The schematic-dominance clause and flat-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-schematic-image-qc] give an injection $B_1\hookrightarrow\Gamma(\mathcal U_T,\mathcal O)$. The given small-etale sheaf isomorphism identifies the last ring with $B_0$. The maps $B_0\to B_1\hookrightarrow B_0$ have composite the identity, since $rq=p$. If $j:B_1\hookrightarrow B_0$ and $i:B_0\to B_1$, then $jij=j$ and injectivity of $j$ gives $ij=\mathrm{id}_{B_1}$; hence $i,j$ are inverse. Therefore $W_T\to T$ is an isomorphism. These inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness of inverses, so glue in the sheaf $W$ to an inverse of $r$.

source.place: Theorem (7.4), locally separated case, printed p.29; Alper Proposition 7.1.1 proof, printed p.36. Both read online, local copies WANTED; explicit stack and Stein adaptations by Q49.

proof.text: Let $a:V\xrightarrow{r^{-1}}W\hookrightarrow A\hookrightarrow Z\times_kV\to Z$. The factorization $g=(h,p)$ gives $ap=h$; step 1 gives uniqueness. Conversely, if $h=ap$, then $hp_1=ap p_1=ap p_2=hp_2$ because the two composites to $V$ are 2-isomorphic on the fibre product and maps to an algebraic space have no nontrivial 2-morphisms. This proves both the injectivity and the stated image criterion, without any hypothesis on geometric fibres.

split_report.summary: Q49 expanded Rydh Theorem (7.4) graph argument from Alper Proposition 7.1.1. No statement change, fibre hypothesis, SGA source, Lean file or build.

lean.statement: theorem stein_submersive_reduced_descent (k : Type u) [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (V : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli V.obj.obj)) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactAlgebraicModuliMap.{u, v, w, u, u + 1, 0, 0} p) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparatedAlgebraicModuliMap p) (hsub : ∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (g : T ⟶ V), Function.Surjective (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd p (discreteModuliMap g.hom.hom))) ∧ ∀ A : Set (ModuliPoints (discreteModuli T.obj.obj)), IsOpen A ↔ IsOpen (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd p (discreteModuliMap g.hom.hom)) ⁻¹' A)) (hstein : IsIso (moduliStructureMap hF.1.1 V p)) (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (hZ : AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q ↦ IsImmersion q.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 Z.obj.obj) (𝟙 Z.obj.obj))) : (∀ a b : V.obj.obj ⟶ Z.obj.obj, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (p.comp (discreteModuliMap a)) (p.comp (discreteModuliMap b))) → a = b) ∧ ∀ h : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli Z.obj.obj), (∃ a : V.obj.obj ⟶ Z.obj.obj, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (p.comp (discreteModuliMap a)) h)) ↔ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsReduced T.left] (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct p p)), Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso ((t.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst p p)).comp h) ((t.comp (moduliTwoFiberSnd p p)).comp h))
lean.note: Agreement on the reduced self fibre product is rendered equivalently by all reduced scheme tests into the actual 2-fibre product. Every reduced test factors through the reduction, and reduced smooth charts of the reduction detect equality into the algebraic-space sheaf. No new reduction object, point-only condition, or geometric-fibre assumption is introduced.
